verdicts.evidence: An AST-based audit of the released code found 19 registered tools, 8 skill documents, implementations for all eight pipeline stages, and a Claude Agent SDK streaming loop with a stepwise tool-use system prompt, but the pipeline was not executed end-to-end, the ReAct loop is delegated to the SDK rather than locally implemented, and the 'first' priority claim was not evaluated.

No benchmark execution was performed; the logbook reports that claude-sonnet-4-20250514 is retired, the 306 original traces and predictions are not released, and the repository lacks an automatic success judge, so the 68.9% accuracy figure cannot be recomputed.

An independent JSONL parser on sp_bench.jsonl found 102 records with 102 unique IDs and queries, 18 categories, 8 stages, and tier counts exactly matching {basic: 40, intermediate: 28, advanced: 21, challenging: 13}, with schema and consistency mutation tests passing.

The released evaluator implements the metric families, but the official dataset lacks CRC-CODEX evaluation inputs, generated quantification outputs, and the complete ground-truth bundle needed to recompute the reported 0.953/0.902/0.368 values; no execution was done.

Four ground-truth files covering 2,013,525 rows pass structural schema checks, but original agent predictions are absent, so the reported 0.681 average similarity cannot be recomputed; the evaluator also has a row-order sensitivity bug noted as a qualification.

overall: The logbook independently verifies the SP-Bench manifest (102 queries, 18 categories, 8 stages, correct tier splits) and partially confirms the released code architecture (19 tools, 8 stage modules, Claude Agent SDK loop), but none of the three numerical performance claims (SP-Bench accuracy, CRC-CODEX metrics, cell-annotation similarity) could be reproduced because original traces, predictions, and evaluation inputs are missing.
